description:
PROBLEM
There is no way to fork a live queue to test a workflow variant and discard it. The motivating scenario (operator, 2026-07-03): "what if I changed the delivery workflow from x to y" — pause a production delivery queue, branch it at a position, run the variant against the branch, compare, discard. TD-009 (docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-009-experimentation-pause-branch-read-as-of.md) designs the mechanics.

CURRENT STATE
- Object-log manifest and segment objects are immutable and per-(tenant,queue): ManifestEntry (crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:539-549), shard_prefix (:582) — already copy-on-write-shaped.
- Leases/epochs are per-queue with a single-active-lease invariant (crates/pqueue-engine/src/control_plane.rs:14,59-89).
- Segment retention/expiry exists per TD-004 and is unaware of cross-queue references.
- read_as_of and intake-blocking pause land in dependency beads.

PROPOSED FIX
Per TD-009 section 3-4: branch(source_shard, at: CommandPosition) -> new QueueKey. Object-log: allocate a new queue identity Q-prime (new prefix + manifest series) whose manifest references the parent's immutable segment objects for sequences <= P (no data copy), diverging with its own segments after; Q-prime acquires its own control-plane lease/epoch (parent fence untouched); emit_change_records=false by default on branches; branch carries a TTL and pins the parent's segments <= P against expiry until the branch is discarded. Relational family: structured capability-unavailable until the ADR-013 rebuild-from-log migration. Document the inherited-lease behavior (reconstructed Leased items expire on the normal clock in the branch) and the shared idempotency namespace <= P.

NON-SCOPE
- Comparison/diff tooling. Automatic branch GC beyond TTL. Relational branch implementation.
title: Branch-at-position: copy-on-write queue fork on the object-log manifest

acceptance: TD-007/TD-006/TD-004 state per-profile upsert/update_fields/reschedule availability with rationale; the upsert-claim race argument is re-derived under the universal ordering; either the hybrid ban is lifted with conformance scenarios covering upsert-during-claim under group commit, or API-003 records the atomic-class requirement for mutable-schedule queues; cascade re-stamped, ddx doc stale clean.
description: ADR-013 (amended 2026-07-05) makes commit ordering universal: log durable -> serving projection applied -> ack. On objectlog/hybrid the serving (memory) projection applies synchronously before ack, so the projection a claim or upsert validates against is current — the upsert-vs-lagging-projection race that motivated TD-007 §2.2's blanket '-ERR pqueue unavailable' for upsert/update_fields/reschedule on the log-then-apply class may now be closable on hybrid profiles. This matters for 7thsense: mutable schedules (FR-46, ingest-then-reschedule) are core to scheduled delivery, and today they are unavailable on the flagship S3-durable profile, forcing atomic-class backends. Decide per profile: which log-then-apply compositions can validate pre-commit against a synchronously-applied serving projection and safely lift the ban; update TD-007 §2.2, TD-006 flavor-difference 5, TD-004, and API-003's scheduled-delivery profile accordingly. If the ban stays for any profile, record the 7thsense topology consequence (mutable-schedule queues must run atomic-class) explicitly in API-003.
title: Re-evaluate log-then-apply upsert/update_fields/reschedule ban under universal commit ordering

description:
PROBLEM
Detail pages and due-work queries need typed range scans and stable cursor pagination over compound indexes. Current typed index lookup is exact-key oriented and does not provide ordered range pages.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement memory and sqlite support for bounded typed range scans over declared compound indexes, including stable ordering by `(scheduled_at ASC, action_id ASC)` and cursor page tokens or an explicit retryable cursor-invalidated error. Expose through the public facade query API added earlier.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- crates/pqueue-projection/src/lib.rs for in-memory projection range scan support.
- crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs for sqlite range scan support.
- crates/pqueue/src/lib.rs and crates/pqueue/tests/hot_projection_queries.rs.

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- Grouped aggregates.
- Bounded mutation.
- Claim-by-query.

ORDERING/TIE-BREAK
Stable ordering and the cursor tie-break must follow the contract decision in pqueue-b1feb686: `action_id` is not a field of the canonical range index, so either the implementation tie-breaks on the internal item id or the test's declared index is extended — implement whichever the contract specifies, and make the test assert that behavior explicitly. In the canonical fixture, ordering by (scheduled_at ASC, internal id ASC) and (scheduled_at ASC, action_id ASC) yield the same page sequence.
title: Implement typed range scans and stable cursor pagination

description:
PROBLEM
There is no way to read a consistent projection state at a historical position — needed for consistent external reads that never touch the hot claim path, and to compare a branched queue against its parent at the fork point (TD-009).

CURRENT STATE
- LogStore::high_water gives the current position cheaply (crates/pqueue-engine/src/compose.rs:113).
- Snapshot-at-position storage exists: write_snapshot/latest_snapshot/read_snapshot (compose.rs:116-123).
- No read_as_of exists; the relational family cannot reconstruct prior state at all today ("nothing to replay", crates/pqueue-postgres/src/relational.rs:983-987) until the ADR-013 migration.

PROPOSED FIX
Per TD-009 section 2: add current_position(shard) -> CommandPosition (thin wrapper over high_water) and read_as_of(shard, position, query) that hydrates from the nearest snapshot <= P, replays read_from up to P into an ephemeral projection, answers the bounded query, and discards. Relational backends return a structured capability-unavailable error until rebuildable-from-log.

NON-SCOPE
- Branch (separate bead). Relational rebuild-from-log migration (ADR-013 derived work).
- No always-on secondary projection; the as-of projection is ephemeral per call.
title: Add current_position and read-as-of-position API

Two contradictory durability contracts share the pqueue-postgres crate: log-authoritative (lib.rs:6-13) vs DB-authoritative (relational.rs:3,983-987,2767 — "pqueue_items is DB-authoritative", "nothing to replay"). Operator decision (2026-07-03): the log is the system of truth, period; the Postgres projection is just another projection; a null-log mode may exist with expected, documented functionality loss.

title: Land ADR-013: the log is the single source of truth; relational projections become rebuildable views

description:
PROBLEM: Manifest deletion needs a durable monotonic watermark distinct from the existing read horizon so recovery can distinguish intentionally reclaimed manifest indices from missing/torn entries, while never skipping live entries or exceeding the durable retention/read floor. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:366 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:367. Dependency ID: pqueue-c33c367e; evaluate and document that this watermark does not rely on owner-fence wiring.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2205 persists `read_horizon.json` as a read-cost watermark; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2331 advances that read horizon only after proving entries are below-floor and reclaimed; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:984 deletes manifest entries without a separate durable deletion watermark that explicitly records the highest physically reclaimed manifest index.
PROPOSED FIX: Add a durable monotonic manifest deletion watermark, or extend the existing durable horizon with explicit deletion semantics, so it survives reopen, only advances over a contiguous reclaimed prefix, and is always strictly bounded by the durable retention/read floor. Reads and recovery must use it to treat absent below-watermark manifest entries as intentional only when the permanent fence protocol remains intact.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, projection storage, or release packaging. Do not use the watermark to hide not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry. Do not make the watermark an authority for retention floor advancement. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.

acceptance:
1. Branch COMMIT is fenced on the SOURCE ownership epoch: an owner that has lost the source epoch to a newer owner CANNOT commit a branch (its commit fails Conflict/rolls back cleanly), proven by a fault-injected ownership-handoff test (superseded owner attempts commit after a new owner's acquire_epoch(source)).
2. Orphan-branch GC is cross-INSTANCE safe on a shared store: a threaded/two-instance test shows GC by the current owner never destroys or unpins a branch a concurrent (now-superseded) creator is committing, and never leaves a missing segment — closing the residual TOCTOU documented at segmented.rs gc_orphaned_branches. The prior single-instance guarantee is preserved.
3. AC-TXN-3 replay-across-restart and atomic branch-existence (branch.json last, uncommitted non-readable) preserved; existing segmented_s3_substrate_tests still green.
4. Codex adversarial review APPROVES the fencing (no residual interleaving that commits or destroys a branch under a superseded owner).
5. rustup run 1.92.0 cargo test -p pqueue-objectlog passes; fmt + clippy -D warnings clean.
description: Codex-confirmed cross-instance concurrency gap surfaced while hardening orphan-branch GC (bead pqueue-74f03d0e, commits 6bcadda5/bfc7b493). The branch COMMIT is NOT fenced on the SOURCE's ownership epoch: in SegmentedObjectLog::branch_attempt (crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs) the commit marker branch.json is written via store_put -> unconditional BlobStore::put (segmented.rs ~848), only the BRANCH's own epoch is acquired (acquire_epoch(&branch), ~1665) — never the source's, and the sole source-side post-copy validation re-reads only the retention FLOOR (~1649), which a new owner's acquire_epoch(source) does NOT move (its fence entry carries retention_floor_through=None). CONSEQUENCE: an owner that has been SUPERSEDED (a newer owner took the source's ownership epoch) can still create AND COMMIT a branch and return Committed. This is a split-brain / ownership-handoff hazard independent of GC (a zombie owner commits a branch on a source it no longer owns), and it is ALSO the residual TOCTOU that prevents orphan-branch GC from being cross-instance-safe: because the commit is unfenced, a GC-only epoch check cannot close the race (the new owner's GC can destroy/unpin a branch the superseded owner is committing, or vice-versa). The single-INSTANCE guarantee (one owner process + background GC thread) is already sound via the create_gc_guard mutual exclusion; this bead covers the CROSS-instance case. NOTE: this modifies the b5cc2bc7 atomic-branch-existence protocol, so it must preserve AC-TXN-3 replay-across-restart and the atomic branch-existence semantics (branch.json written LAST; uncommitted branch non-readable).
title: objectlog: fence branch COMMIT on source ownership epoch (cross-instance superseded-owner safety)

OUT-OF-SCOPE

description:
Snorri/Cayce needs pqueue to provide an authoritative StateStore boundary before Snorri can replace Cayce's internal workflow runtime in production.

Current evidence from sibling snorri, run against pqueue revision a7401c1:
- `cargo run -p snorri-spike-pqueue -- --source-audit --format markdown` passes its audit harness but reports blocking gaps: no public vectorized claimed-work commit, public upsert/ack/finalize do not accept caller request ids, public ack is item-id shaped instead of lease-token claim-ref shaped, backend data-plane envelopes still build `request_id: None`, `QueueIdempotencyCache` is documented as not wired through push/claim/finalize, RESP is worker/interoperability only, and non-work side records/recovery reads are missing.
- `cargo run -p snorri-spike-pqueue -- --prototype --format markdown` proves the public Rust facade can express Snorri input/state/audit/outbox/await records, but only as multiple public operations: upsert input, claim input, upsert state, push audit, upsert outbox, upsert await, ack input. That is not one recoverable transition boundary.

Required pqueue capability:
Expose a public Rust API for a vectorized claimed-work commit suitable for Snorri transition commits. Each vector entry must atomically validate a lease-token-bearing claim reference, apply bounded opaque non-work side-record writes for workflow state and audit, apply ordinary queue lifecycle writes for dispatchable outbox/await/timer work as needed, advance or validate a caller-supplied instance/state fence, finalize the input claim, and return a per-entry outcome. The API must accept caller-supplied request ids so Snorri can derive stable transition request ids from durable workflow inputs and rely on retained replay/conflict/expired outcomes.

Detailed requirements:
- Public Rust facade exposes a native claimed-work commit operation, not only hidden engine ports.
- Commit request includes caller request id or per-entry transition request id; same body replays, different body conflicts, expired idempotency metadata returns a structural expired outcome.
- Commit entries carry a claim reference with item id, lease token, lease expiry, and item version/fence. Public finalization must not depend only on item id.
- Commit validates claim authority and state/item fence inside the same durable boundary as side-record writes and input finalization.
- Backend command-envelope construction propagates request ids instead of building data-plane envelopes with `request_id: None` for this path.
- QueueIdempotencyCache or equivalent retained request-id machinery is wired into the accepted data-plane commit path.
- Side records intended for authoritative state/audit are not ordinary claimable work. Provide generic non-work opaque records, an equivalent documented non-work convention with conformance tests, or a capability-declared adapter-owned table boundary. Outbox effects, due timers, and awaits may remain ordinary queue lifecycle records when claim/finalize semantics are intended.
- Capability descriptors must let Snorri reject unsupported backends before activation: atomic transition commit, vectorized commit, lease validation, retained commit idempotency, non-work side records, authoritative recovery reads, delayed awaits/timers where advertised, and clear durability/consistency boundary.
- Recovery/explain reads expose enough committed records to decide retry/replay and explain instance state: transition request id, workflow instance key/fence, consumed input event id, side-record writes, outbox/await/timer records, and per-entry commit status.
- RESP is explicitly out of scope for authoritative Snorri StateStore MVP unless it grows an equivalent Rust-finalizable claim/ref and request-id commit boundary. RESP can remain worker/interoperability surface.

In-scope areas:

description:

ROOT CAUSE: `crates/pqueue-service/src/runtime.rs:93` through `crates/pqueue-service/src/runtime.rs:106` define runtime config with only `postgres_database_url`; `crates/pqueue-service/src/runtime.rs:146` only reads `PQUEUE_POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL`; `crates/pqueue-service/src/runtime.rs:167` through `crates/pqueue-service/src/runtime.rs:175` returns `ReadinessCheck::Ready` for `ObjectLogSqliteProjection` without checking S3-compatible object storage, SQLite projection path, segment settings, credentials, or Postgres control-plane configuration.

PROPOSED FIX: Extend `RuntimeConfig` and runtime tests to parse and validate the object-log environment contract: `PQUEUE_OBJECT_LOG_ENDPOINT`, `PQUEUE_OBJECT_LOG_BUCKET`, `PQUEUE_OBJECT_LOG_REGION`, `PQUEUE_OBJECT_LOG_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `PQUEUE_OBJECT_LOG_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `PQUEUE_OBJECT_LOG_SEGMENT_MAX_COMMANDS`, `PQUEUE_SQLITE_PROJECTION_DIR`, and required Postgres control-plane URL. GOVERNING ARTIFACTS: Parent bead `pqueue-3546063c`; `docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-004-s3-object-log-sqlite-projection-mode.md`; `docs/helix/04-build/DEPLOYMENT-READINESS.md`; `docs/deployment/container-runtime-contract.md`.

acceptance:

description:
PRE-EXISTING durability hazard surfaced during codex review of the AC-TXN-3 mixed-replay work (pqueue-db60657d), NOT introduced by it (the pre-bead per-entry commit_locked path had the same window; the db60657d overlay actually FIXED it for the in-memory backend).

PROBLEM: a single commit_transition whose entries enqueue TWO lifecycle items sharing the SAME unique typed-index key can, on a RELATIONAL backend (sqlite/postgres), append its envelope batch DURABLY and then FAIL during apply_live: relational ProjectionStore::index_validate_push is a no-op (crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs ~9067), so the collision is not caught at validation; typed-index uniqueness is enforced only at apply time (relational.rs ~1452-1473). commit_locked_batch (crates/pqueue-engine/src/compose.rs ~1861) appends to the durable log BEFORE apply, and the projection tx rolls back while the log append stays durable -> the batch is durable-but-unappliable -> every reopen re-hits it -> RECOVERY POISON for that shard.

The in-memory backend is safe (its index_validate_push + the db60657d committed_pushes overlay catch the collision at validation, returning Conflict before append). Only the relational family is exposed.

SCOPE: make the relational path reject an in-commit duplicate unique typed-index key at VALIDATION (before the durable append) — either by implementing relational index_validate_push to check the in-commit committed_pushes set + the DB, or by a batch preflight — so a colliding commit_transition rejects the entry (Conflict) instead of appending an unappliable batch. Then a conformance test: a two-entry commit_transition with colliding unique lifecycle-push keys on sqlite_log/postgres rejects the second entry and leaves the log appliable + reopenable (no poison).

description:
PROBLEM: A stale owner can retain an in-memory `next_manifest_index` for an index that later falls below the durable floor and is reclaimed. If reclamation deletes that index outright, the stale owner can later write to the freed address and false-ack. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:365. Dependency ID: pqueue-c33c367e; the fix must not depend on pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring unless it proves a substrate-level bounded-staleness invariant.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1324 keeps the seal path on an in-memory cached tail and intentionally avoids listing the manifest before every seal; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:976 uses create-only `put_if_absent` as the manifest CAS; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:984 deletes manifest entries by removing both legacy and authoritative head objects. Those behaviors combine to let a dormant writer target a reclaimed index without first discovering the new floor.
PROPOSED FIX: Wire the reclaim-time fence into the seal/commit path so a stale owner with a cached `next_manifest_index` at a reclaimed below-floor address cannot ack. The stale write must fail as `EpochFenced` or `Conflict`, and the path must preserve the hot-path design choice of not listing the manifest before every seal.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, projection storage, or release packaging. Do not accept tail-validate/delete rollback as a substitute for a permanent fence. Do not rely on pqueue-c33c367e unless this bead proves and documents the bounded-window invariant. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.
title: objectlog: reject stale cached-tail writers after manifest reclaim

acceptance: pqueue's root Cargo.toml patches kafka-protocol to the bounded fork (easel/kafka-protocol-rs, branch heimq-bound-array-capacity); Cargo.lock records the git fork as the source for kafka-protocol, not the crates.io registry; a CI check or test asserts that source so the protection cannot silently regress; cargo check --workspace and cargo test -p pqueue-server stay green; the separate RUSTSEC-2024-0436 paste advisory is either ignored with a written rationale in deny.toml or resolved.
description:
pqueue-server boots the embedded Kafka-compatible surface (crates/pqueue-server/src/lib.rs:22, heimq::server::Server, plus fjord-broker), so it decodes Kafka wire frames from clients. It decodes them with the UNPATCHED upstream kafka-protocol 0.15.1 from crates.io (Cargo.lock: source = registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index).

heimq already fixed this. heimq's root Cargo.toml carries:

  # Pinned fork of kafka-protocol 0.15.1 that bounds Array/CompactArray decode
  # pre-allocation to the remaining buffer (fixes a remotely-triggerable OOM DoS:
  # a small request with a huge array-count field caused a multi-GB Vec::with_capacity
  # before reading any element). Upstream is unbounded in all versions (0.15-0.17).
  [patch.crates-io]
  kafka-protocol = { git = "https://github.com/easel/kafka-protocol-rs", branch = "heimq-bound-array-capacity" }

But cargo only honours [patch.crates-io] from the TOP-LEVEL workspace root. When pqueue depends on heimq by git, heimq's patch section is ignored entirely. So heimq-the-project is protected and pqueue-the-embedder is not, silently, with no build warning and no lockfile hint beyond the registry source line.

IMPACT: a remotely-triggerable OOM DoS on any pqueue-server that exposes the embedded Kafka surface. An attacker sends a small request whose array-count field is huge; the decoder does Vec::with_capacity(count) before reading a single element. This is NOT the paste advisory -- it is strictly more serious and is not reported by cargo-deny at all.

FIX: add the same [patch.crates-io] stanza to pqueue's root Cargo.toml, with a comment pointing at heimq's rationale and heimq-bb299c68, so pqueue resolves the bounded fork. Verify with:
  rg -A2 '^name = "kafka-protocol"' Cargo.lock   # source must be the git fork, not registry
Then add a regression check so this cannot silently regress: assert in CI (or a small test) that the resolved kafka-protocol source is the fork. A lockfile assertion is enough; the failure mode is silent, so a guard is the point.

NOTE it does NOT clear RUSTSEC-2024-0436 (paste unmaintained): heimq's own Cargo.lock still contains paste, because the fork is still based on kafka-protocol 0.15.1 which depends on it. That advisory is a separate decision -- either an advisories.ignore entry with a written rationale, or wait for an upstream kafka-protocol that drops paste (upstream is unbounded in 0.15-0.17, so a version bump alone does not solve the OOM either).

DO NOT "fix heimq" for this. heimq is already correct. The defect is that the protection does not propagate to embedders, which is a property of cargo's patch resolution, not of heimq's code. Consider also asking heimq to document this for embedders, or to vendor the bound inside heimq-broker so it travels with the crate rather than living in a workspace-root patch.
title: pqueue-server decodes untrusted Kafka frames with the UNPATCHED kafka-protocol (heimq's OOM bound does not propagate)

description:

Parent bead pqueue-67cfe2b6 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: Partial expiry must not advance manifest deletion state past below-floor entries that have not yet been deleted, because later full expiry still needs accurate manifest metadata. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec; evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring before implementation and document whether it would allow any cheaper delete-only variant.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1996 states that expire_segments_through deletes only segment objects; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1998 deliberately does not delete manifest tombstones; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2028 advances only the read horizon after reclamation; without a separate conservative manifest deletion watermark, partial expiry could hide undeleted below-floor manifest entries.
PROPOSED FIX: Add partial-expiry-safe manifest deletion bookkeeping that advances only through a contiguous prefix of physically deleted, unpinned, below-floor manifest objects. Ensure interrupted or bounded expiry leaves undeleted entries visible to later expiry and recovery.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not hide not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, or projection storage. Do not implement a delete-only compaction on the current index-CAS protocol. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- TestInterruptedManifestReclaimRecovery: after an interrupted reclamation pass, reopening the log preserves all undeleted below-floor manifest entries and the next reclamation resumes from the durable watermark.
- TestManifestDeletionWatermarkContiguousPrefixOnly: the deletion watermark advances only across a contiguous prefix of confirmed-deleted manifest objects and never over gaps.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.
title: objectlog: make partial manifest expiry watermark-safe: part 2

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead pqueue-7a276379 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 2 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: A stale objectlog owner can restart with a cached reclaimed `next_manifest_index`; if reclaimed-index fence state is only process-local, reopen/recovery can permit a false ack at a historical index. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:365. Dependency ID: pqueue-c33c367e; this child must not depend on pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring unless it proves a substrate-level bounded-staleness invariant.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:984 deletes manifest entries by removing both legacy and authoritative head objects; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:976 uses create-only `put_if_absent` as the manifest CAS; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1324 keeps seal on an in-memory recovered tail and intentionally avoids manifest listing before every seal; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2220 reloads only the durable read-horizon blob, so any reclaimed-index fence state that is not persisted there or in an equivalent recovery-visible object is lost across reopen.
PROPOSED FIX: Persist reclaimed-index fence state in a recovery-visible objectlog substrate object and reload it during open/recovery before seal can accept a stale cached index. The stale writer must reject with `EpochFenced` or `Conflict` before writing a segment or manifest entry, while preserving the O(1) seal hot path shape from docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:365.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, projection storage, or release packaging. Do not accept tail-validate/delete rollback as a substitute for a permanent fence. Do not rely on pqueue-c33c367e unless this bead proves and documents the bounded-window invariant. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- TestRustReopenFenceGate: run `cargo +1.92.0 test -p pqueue-objectlog --test segmented_s3_substrate_tests TestPermanentFenceSurvivesReopen TestReopenFenceReloadsBeforeSeal -- --nocapture` or the exact Rust test symbols added for this child bead.
- TestWorkspaceQualityGate: run `cargo +1.92.0 fmt --all --check`, `cargo +1.92.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.92.0 test --workspace`, `go test ./...` and record not-applicable if no Go module/packages exist, and `lefthook run pre-commit` or record missing lefthook config/tool as an operator-required gate failure.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM: The hybrid-async perf suite pushes one uniform payload string through a single sequential producer/consumer at one resident count and one repetition, so it cannot emit release-grade evidence across scale, cache state, concurrency, or workload shape.
ROOT CAUSE: spec() at crates/pqueue-server/tests/performance_object_log_hybrid_tests.rs:92 hardcodes the payload with no size/key/retry/error distribution; exercise_profile at crates/pqueue-server/tests/performance_object_log_hybrid_tests.rs:183 is a single sequential loop with no concurrency or cache-state control; run_suite at crates/pqueue-server/tests/performance_object_log_hybrid_tests.rs:669 reads one PQUEUE_HYBRID_RESIDENT and runs each backend once with no repetitions.
PROPOSED FIX: (a) add a deterministic seeded workload generator (seed=0, documented in docs/perf) driving spec() with pinned payload-size, client_item_key cardinality, retry-injection, and error-injection distributions; (b) add warm-cache (projection pre-touched) vs cold-cache (fresh backend open) run variants; (c) sweep concurrency via N tokio producer/consumer tasks (new PQUEUE_HYBRID_CONCURRENCY) and load/claim batch via existing *_BATCH env vars, emitting one ProfileRun per (cache,concurrency,batch) cell; (d) parametrize resident across {10000,100000,1000000,10000000} gated by an RSS/capacity guard that skips-with-log any scale exceeding the machine budget; (e) run >=5 repetitions per release cell and record median plus coefficient-of-variation with a documented outlier-trim policy.
NON-SCOPE: the hot-path performance fix (child 'Close hybrid-async hot-path gap'); bounded-debt/segment/attribution gates (child 'Hybrid-async perf gates + profile attribution'); running the release matrix and emitting final docs (child 'Emit release-grade hybrid-async evidence'); release version bump.
GATE SUBSTITUTION: this is a Rust/cargo crate with no go.mod or lefthook; the 'go test' gate is `cargo test -p pqueue-server` and the 'lefthook' pre-commit gate is `cargo fmt --check`.

description:
Create the missing pqueue HELIX contract surface for delivery-style application clients. pqueue already defines the core queue primitives in docs/helix/02-design/contracts/API-001-native-client-interface.md: BatchPush, BatchUpdate, dynamic gate_keys, BatchClaim, BatchRenewLeases, BatchFinalize, PurgeItems, and active-scope discovery. API-002 already owns privileged operator archive/retention. The missing upstream contract is not a new queue primitive and must not add Seventh Sense, 7snx, SES, suppression, sender readiness, provider idempotency, or downstream quota semantics to pqueue core.

Add a workload integration profile contract under docs/helix/02-design/contracts/ that explains how an application delivery engine should use the native pqueue primitives. The first profile should cover scheduled batch delivery generically, not as a 7snx-specific API. It should define queue creation recommendations, producer obligations, worker obligations, finalize outcome mapping, dynamic gate usage, and archive/retention boundaries.

Also tighten API-001 so adapter authors know exactly what a claimed item returns. The claimed item response shape should explicitly include item_id, client_item_key, lease_token, lease_expires_at, item_version, priority, not_before, group_key, payload, metadata, and gate_keys when applicable.

In-scope files:
- docs/helix/02-design/contracts/API-001-native-client-interface.md
- docs/helix/02-design/contracts/API-003-workload-integration-profiles.md (new)
- docs/helix/01-frame/prd.md (small cross-reference only if useful)
- docs/helix/03-test/test-plans/* (only if the project requires a traceability/test-plan update for the new contract)

Out-of-scope:
- crates/** implementation code
- SES-specific, 7snx-specific, or Seventh Sense-specific APIs
- pqueue-owned downstream rate limiting or quota enforcement
- pqueue-owned delivery state machines, sender readiness, suppression decisions, provider result normalization, or provider idempotency keys
- Changes to API-002 archive/retention behavior beyond a cross-reference from the new profile

Design constraints:
- Keep pqueue domain-neutral. The profile may use generic examples such as tenant, sender, domain, provider, or batch compatibility keys, but those examples must remain opaque caller-owned metadata/gate keys.
- Preserve the existing PRD non-goal: pqueue does not enforce downstream API rate limits; callers pace with max_items, claim cadence, not_before, group selection, retries, and caller-owned gates.
- Make the profile executable by an adapter author who has no context from external chat or 7snx docs.
title: Define workload integration profile contract for delivery-style clients

description:
PROBLEM
`SqliteRelationalBackend` still describes the relational projection as DB-authoritative and its reopen path as replay-free, so the sqlite relational family cannot be rebuilt from the durable log tail.
ROOT CAUSE
`crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs:1691-1693, 4039-4040, 8425-8428, 9330-9335` still says the item projection is already durable, the backend is DB-authoritative, and recovery only repopulates control-plane state and counters.
PROPOSED FIX
Persist the sqlite relational applied high-water, make `recovery_high_water` return the applied position, and update the reopen/composed recovery path so sqlite relational state is restored by replaying the durable log tail instead of treating `pqueue_items` as authoritative.
NON-SCOPE
postgres family changes, shared compose wiring, conformance-suite expansion, docs wording cleanup, and the `pqueue-b59f4897` TOCTOU prerequisite fix.
title: Sqlite relational recover-from-log

acceptance: Retry-exhaustion emits a terminal Failed record with terminal_at; cohort finalize/expiry emit per-member terminal records; synthesis remains exhaustive over QueueCommand variants; tests cover both.
description: Review of 7d62de3: records are synthesized from the command alone (command.rs:786-808). (a) finalize_state(kind, None) always maps Retry->Pending, so a retry finalize that actually exhausts max_attempts and lands terminal Failed emits a Pending record with no terminal_at — that item's terminal transition is absent from history, breaking CL-1 and the cayce delivery-history use case. (b) CohortFinalize/CohortExpired emit one null-item queue-scoped record, so cohort-finalized items get no per-item terminal record. Resolve applied state at emission time (attempt counts, cohort membership) or enrich the CommandEnvelope so synthesis is faithful. Add tests for retry-exhaustion and cohort-terminal emission.
title: Fix change-record synthesis fidelity: retry-exhaustion terminal state + per-item cohort records (TD-008 CL-1)

1. TestBranchInheritanceAfterManifestDeletion: branches from trimmed sources inherit floors, read their own live view, preserve the seed-floor `seq == f` edge, and never GET a physically deleted source manifest or segment object.

description:
PROBLEM: The head-CAS and physical deletion changes have high blast radius across branch creation, restart recovery, conformance, SQLite/objectlog integration, and release evidence; landing the protocol without integration hardening risks regressions in AC-TXN-3, behind-image fail-closed behavior, branch inheritance, and retention-floor semantics. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374 and docs/helix/03-test/test-plans/TP-003-verification-acceptance-criteria.md:224. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec; evaluate pqueue-c33c367e interaction first and carry that conclusion into release notes.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1693 snapshots source epoch by recovering the source manifest; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1755 seeds inherited branch floors; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1772 copies live source manifest entries; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1826 recovers branch manifest state before acquiring the branch epoch. These paths assume manifest entries remain the branch/recovery substrate and must be made correct after below-floor physical deletion and head-based tail recovery.
PROPOSED FIX: Update branch creation, branch GC, restart recovery, objectlog+sqlite integration, conformance tests, and release documentation so the full protocol works end-to-end. Run Codex adversarial review on the final fencing/commit protocol and fold blocking findings before declaring the parent bead complete.
NON-SCOPE: Do not introduce new queue semantics or user-facing API changes. Do not relax existing branch atomicity, orphan GC, source pin, retention floor, or fail-closed guarantees. Do not skip objectlog, sqlite, engine, conformance, fmt, clippy, lefthook, go test, or Codex adversarial review gates. Do not pursue this work unless manifest object-count/storage growth is operationally real for very long-lived, high-write, trimming-enabled queues.

description:
PROBLEM
Snorri's saga/workflow-state design (epic pqueue-2201fd37, "Snorri authoritative-commit boundary") is meant to let most single-transaction saga-step work happen INSIDE pqueue's own atomic commit boundary (CommitTransitionPort: validate a lease/version claim ref, write opaque side records, enqueue next-step lifecycle items, advance a caller instance/state fence, and finalize the consumed input claim -- all atomically, per entry). This is fully implemented and advertised on pqueue-memory (via the generic composed backend) and pqueue-sqlite's relational family (crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs:5731, all capabilities true, DurabilityClass::Atomic).

Postgres -- the actual production/Lakebase deployment target for Snorri -- does NOT implement it. Both PostgresBackend (crates/pqueue-postgres/src/lib.rs:904) and PostgresRelationalBackend (crates/pqueue-postgres/src/relational.rs:3455) have empty `impl CommitTransitionPort for X {}` blocks inheriting the Unavailable default, and WriteSideRecords/AdvanceInstanceFence are explicitly rejected with a code comment noting "the durable parity slice is deferred (C9)". This is not an architectural blocker: both postgres backends already report `DurabilityClass::Atomic` (their `Backend::write` unit of work already commits atomically) -- the atomic-transaction primitive exists, only the saga-commit orchestration layer on top of it (side-record/instance-fence tables + the vectorized per-entry commit method + RecoveryReadPort + honest commit_capabilities()) is unported.

Until this closes, Snorri cannot run its saga/state-machine model against Lakebase in production -- only against sqlite, which is not the deployment target.

EPIC OUTCOME
PostgresRelationalBackend (scope of the flavor(s) decided by the first child bead) implements CommitTransitionPort and RecoveryReadPort with real behavior matching sqlite-relational's, verified by the SAME shared pqueue-conformance scenario sqlite/memory already pass (epic pqueue-54039317, dependency of this epic) -- not a new bespoke test file.

SEQUENCING NOTE
This epic depends on pqueue-d2f0b763 (wire the shared commit-transition conformance scenario into every backend) landing first, so this epic's implementation beads are verified against the real shared harness from the start rather than yet another one-off test file that would need migrating later.

NON-SCOPE
- pqueue-objectlog parity (eventual-apply; cannot offer one atomic transition boundary by construction -- out of scope for this epic, may warrant its own future decision doc if ever needed).
- Any Snorri/Cayce-side code.
- RESP surface for this boundary (explicitly out of scope per epic pqueue-2201fd37).

description:
PROBLEM
A terminal item reaped before its terminal change record is durably emitted silently drops the terminal transition from downstream history — the subtlest correctness rule in TD-008. Separately, emission lag must be observable so operators can see history debt.

CURRENT STATE
- Terminal reap is governed by terminal_retention_ms alone (crates/pqueue-core/src/domain.rs:599,631; purge/tombstone paths in the relational stores).
- Debt-metric pattern to mirror: TD-004 async-apply debt metrics.
- Emission cursor lands with the engine foundation bead.

PROPOSED FIX
Per TD-008 Retention section: reap frontier = min(terminal_at + retention, emission_cursor_position) — a terminal item past retention is NOT reaped while the emission cursor is behind its terminal record; it becomes reapable once the cursor durably passes it. Queues with emit_change_records=false keep the pure retention frontier. Add emission_lag_commands and emission_oldest_unemitted_age_ms metrics, plus a resident-terminal-count metric so the 1h-retention memory cost is visible.

NON-SCOPE
- Sink/transport (sibling bead). Retention default change (already its own bead).
title: Couple terminal reap to the emission frontier and expose emission lag metrics

description:
PROBLEM
Snorri/Cayce needs hot workflow visibility before completed actions are archived to Niflheim/ClickHouse. Current pqueue projection reads (`peek`, `claimed`, `live_items`, `metrics`, exact typed index lookups) are not enough for operational reporting over scheduled workflow actions while the queue is hot. The superseded task pqueue-630dbeaa captured the full requirement set: domain-neutral hot indexed projection records, range/detail queries, hourly/grouped aggregates, numeric buckets, safe bounded mutation, claim-due-work-by-query, backend capability advertising, docs, and public facade tests.

CURRENT STATE
pqueue already has typed indexes (`QueueIndex`), exact typed lookup via `IndexQueryPort`, item `live_items`, and projection-backed claim/finalize paths. It does not have a domain-neutral public query substrate for typed range scans, grouping, cursor pagination, side/projection records, or bounded updates. No governing `api-hot-projection-query-surface` document exists yet; `rg` only finds the old bead.

EPIC OUTCOME
Deliver the generic pqueue substrate Snorri can build on without adding Snorri-specific workflow semantics: contract docs, public query types, backend capability advertising, memory/sqlite implementations, public Rust facade tests over the six scheduled-action fixture records, and final workspace gates.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement Snorri/Cayce APIs, MCP tools, source-map rendering, open-rate policy semantics, Niflheim/ClickHouse archival analytics, arbitrary SQL/JSONPath execution, or RESP reporting before the Rust/query substrate is proven.

SIDE/PROJECTION RECORDS (DEFERRED)
The contract (pqueue-b1feb686) defines side/projection-record semantics and a `side_record_query` capability flag, but no bead in this epic implements side-record storage or queries. Every backend advertises `side_record_query` unavailable and returns the structured unsupported error. If Snorri needs queryable non-claimable records, open a follow-up epic; do not bolt side-record implementation onto these beads.

SEQUENCING NOTE
The child beads are intentionally serialized (contract -> types -> fixture -> range scans -> aggregates -> mutation -> claim-by-query -> conformance -> docs) because every implementation bead extends the same crates/pqueue/tests/hot_projection_queries.rs fixture file. Do not parallelize them.

description:
PROBLEM
CommitTransitionPort/RecoveryReadPort (the Snorri authoritative-commit boundary, epic pqueue-2201fd37) was shipped with bespoke, per-backend tests instead of scenarios in the shared pqueue-conformance "no-stub" harness (crates/pqueue-conformance/src/lib.rs). ConformanceCore/ConformanceBackend have zero references to CommitTransitionPort, RecoveryReadPort, WriteSideRecords, or AdvanceInstanceFence. sqlite-relational got 7 bespoke tests (crates/pqueue-sqlite/tests/relational_commit.rs), memory got 14 (crates/pqueue-memory/src/tests.rs). Postgres (both PostgresBackend and PostgresRelationalBackend, which both inherit the Unavailable default via empty `impl CommitTransitionPort for X {}`) got ZERO tests -- not even a negative/explicit-decline test. This is how a whole capability silently shipped with no postgres coverage: nothing ever ran against postgres to fail.

The project already has the right convention for optional/capability-gated ports elsewhere: the hot-projection substrate (API-004, epic pqueue-45e13e4d) added `hot_projection_capabilities_are_explicit` on postgres, which asserts the backend honestly advertises QueryCapabilityFlags::default() rather than silently omitting the check. That convention was not applied when CommitTransitionPort shipped.

EPIC OUTCOME
Every backend in the workspace (pqueue-memory composed, pqueue-sqlite log + relational, pqueue-postgres log + relational, pqueue-objectlog) is required, by a shared scenario in pqueue-conformance, to either (a) pass the full commit-transition behavioral suite when it advertises the capability, or (b) pass an explicit-decline + capability-flag-consistency check when it does not. A future backend that silently ships a stubbed CommitTransitionPort impl fails CI automatically, without anyone remembering to write a bespoke test file.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement CommitTransitionPort for postgres or objectlog in this epic -- that is the separate epic "Bring postgres to Snorri commit-transition parity with sqlite-relational". This epic is test-infrastructure only; postgres/objectlog should still show capability=false and pass the harness's decline path when this epic closes.

description:
PROBLEM: Reopen/recovery does not yet make the durable manifest deletion watermark a durable read-floor input, so later read-path enforcement can lose the below-floor boundary after restart. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec. Evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring before implementation and document whether it changes the watermark design.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2028 advances only the read horizon after reclamation, while docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374 require deleted manifest addresses to remain a durable read-floor constraint across reopen/recovery.
PROPOSED FIX: Thread the manifest deletion watermark into the durable reopen/recovery state so recovered readers reconstruct the same read floor that existed after manifest deletion. Preserve behavior for still-present manifest entries until the watermark is durably advanced, and record the pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence evaluation in the implementation notes or test comments.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not hide not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, or projection storage. Do not implement a delete-only compaction on the current index-CAS protocol. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.
title: objectlog: persist manifest deletion watermark through reopen recovery

description: The 10M hybrid release diagnostic now consistently reaches objectlog/sqlite.hot_claim_finalize, but it times out there before emitting the phase row. Three 2026-07-02 8m guarded runs with PQUEUE_LEDGER_DIR=docs/perf/evidence/hybrid-scale PQUEUE_PERF_ENV=1 PQUEUE_HYBRID_RESIDENT=10000000 timeout 8m cargo test -p pqueue-server --release --test performance_object_log_hybrid_tests performance_object_log_hybrid_release_10m -- --ignored --nocapture timed out during sqlite.hot_claim_finalize. Earlier work reduced recovery reopen I/O and added S3-style cost counters, and candidate-scan/rowid-range update experiments passed focused tests but did not clear the 10M timeout. The remaining bottleneck is narrower than object-log batching: direct SQLite claim/finalize at 10M, likely render_claimed/per-item token handling, per-batch row materialization, or remaining large write/read amplification after claim selection.
notes: Resolved 2026-07-02: instrumented sqlite.hot_claim_finalize with per-window claim/outcome/finalize timing and process I/O. description:
PROBLEM: Manifest object count cannot be bounded while `recover_manifest` treats append-only `manifest/{index}` objects as the authoritative tail and while `BlobStore` exposes only create-only `put_if_absent` CAS. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec; evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring before implementation and document whether it changes the deletion safety envelope.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:55 defines `BlobStore` without a linearizable conditional-update/head primitive; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:60 makes create-only `put_if_absent` the only CAS; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1010 derives `(next_seq,next_manifest_index,current_epoch)` by listing manifest keys and reading the max key; docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:21 explains that freeing an old index lets a stale writer win create-only CAS at that address.
PROPOSED FIX: Add a versioned permanent manifest head object, e.g. `{shard}/manifest_head.json`, carrying current epoch, next index/sequence, retention floor, and an opaque CAS/version token. Extend all `BlobStore` implementations and S3/MinIO tests with conditional read/update semantics for that head. Make recovery prefer the head and keep a backward-compatible bootstrap path from existing append-only manifests. Preserve TD-004 ack-after-manifest semantics and do not physically delete manifest entries in this child.
NON-SCOPE: Do not implement physical deletion of manifest entries in this child. Do not change branch copy semantics beyond reading/recovering the head-compatible tail. Do not relax AC-TXN-3 replay, behind-image fail-closed, branch inheritance, retention floor, or epoch fencing. Do not depend on an unproven wall-clock staleness bound; pqueue-c33c367e must be evaluated first, not assumed. Do not squash/rebase/filter DDX attempt history.

acceptance:
1. Focused tests prove the object-storage append/group-commit interface encourages or requires batched operation for normal data-plane traffic: a multi-command release-like workload must produce mean_commands_per_segment > 1 and max_commands_per_segment > 1 before acknowledgement.
2. A guardrail test fails if a normal object-storage data-plane path can force one command per segment without an explicit low-volume/control/sync override.
3. Release evidence rows include object-storage file/object count, segment bytes, total stored bytes, mean/max object size, storage-utilization ratio versus configured target segment size, PUT/LIST/GET counts, and an estimated S3-style request plus retained-storage cost with price inputs recorded in the row.
4. PQUEUE_LEDGER_DIR=docs/perf/evidence/hybrid-scale PQUEUE_PERF_ENV=1 PQUEUE_HYBRID_RESIDENT=1000000 cargo test -p pqueue-server --release --test performance_object_log_hybrid_tests performance_object_log_hybrid_release_10m -- --ignored --nocapture passes with bars_met=true, objectlog_hybrid_mean_commands_per_segment > 1, objectlog_hybrid_max_commands_per_segment > 1, and populated object-store utilization/cost fields.
5. A capped 10M preflight command, PQUEUE_LEDGER_DIR=docs/perf/evidence/hybrid-scale PQUEUE_PERF_ENV=1 PQUEUE_HYBRID_RESIDENT=10000000 timeout 15m cargo test -p pqueue-server --release --test performance_object_log_hybrid_tests performance_object_log_hybrid_release_10m -- --ignored --nocapture, must not spend the majority of sampled CPU in recover_manifest/walk_keys/current_epoch on the hot path; if it times out, capture perf evidence proving the dominant bottleneck moved away from manifest listing and leave pqueue-d6453cdd open. If it completes, bars_met must be true and object-store utilization/cost fields must be populated.
6. cargo fmt --check passes.
description:
The 10M hybrid-async release evidence run for pqueue-d6453cdd was stopped after ~60 minutes because perf sampling showed the hot thread spending CPU in std::path::Components::next under pqueue_objectlog::segmented::walk_keys -> LocalFsBlobStore::list -> SegmentedObjectLog::recover_manifest, called from SegmentedObjectLog::current_epoch/seal during ComposedBackend claim/finalize. The release harness uses 500-member push/claim/finalize batches, so 10M members should be roughly 60k durable batch commands, not 10M per-member records. However the object-storage segmented log produced one command per segment at scale (mean_commands_per_segment=1.0 in current evidence). That granularity is unacceptable for object storage.

Correct design constraint: objectlog/hybrid-async must preserve object-log durability. Do not route normal data-plane commands through a local transaction that is acknowledged before object-log durability. Instead, normal data-plane traffic must wait for durable object-log group commit and should be batched by interface and implementation so one command per segment is very unlikely under load. Rare explicit sync/control flushes (for example an operator sync-now once an hour) are acceptable, but must be identified in metrics and must not dominate object count, request count, file size utilization, or cost.

In scope: change the command append/group-commit interface and hybrid-async storage design so high-volume release workloads append multiple commands per object-storage segment before acknowledgement; make single-command segment creation an explicit low-volume/control-path override rather than the default; add object-store file/object count, bytes, utilization, PUT/LIST/GET request counts, and S3-style cost estimates to release evidence; add tests/gates preventing one-command segment collapse for normal data-plane traffic. Out of scope: weakening the 10M release performance gates, accepting one-command object-log segments as release evidence, or acknowledging normal traffic from a local-only transaction before object-log commit.
title: Prevent object-storage log one-command segment collapse

description:
PROBLEM
Snorri/Cayce needs hot workflow visibility before completed actions are archived to Niflheim/ClickHouse. Current pqueue projection reads (`peek`, `claimed`, `live_items`, `metrics`, exact typed index lookups) are not enough for Cayce-style operational reporting over scheduled workflow actions while the queue is hot.

7th Sense reference shape inspected from `/Users/erik/Projects/7thsense/master`:
- `interfaces/graphile/postgraphile/src/services/jobActionsChartService.ts` groups hot/cold action rows by `toStartOfHour(scheduledTimestamp)`, `status`, `suppressedByRecycling`, and `schedulerAlgorithm`; segments `engagementProbability`; and reports recycling details.
- `infrastructure/postgres/src/main/scala/ss/postgres/quill/QuillScheduledActionsPersistence.scala` creates scheduled actions, claims due actions by `jobId/type/status/scheduledTimestamp`, calculates hourly/status/algorithm/engagement buckets, counts pending/remaining actions, and applies status-update rules for engagement class and open-rate filter membership.
- `interfaces/graphile/db/postgres/dump.sql` defines `jobs_scheduled_actions` with indexes on `(job_id)`, `(job_id, scheduled_timestamp, status)`, `(parent_job_id, target_key)`, and `delivery_id`.

Snorri should expose the workflow query language to Cayce/MCP, but pqueue must provide the generic hot indexed projection substrate underneath it. pqueue must stay domain-neutral: do not add Snorri-specific workflow semantics, source-map concepts, Cayce open-rate vocabulary, or long-retention analytics. It should provide typed indexed record/query primitives with bounded aggregation and safe mutation semantics that Snorri can use to implement its own workflow visibility API.

REQUIRED HOT RECORD SHAPE
The contract must support queue items and non-claimable side/projection records carrying typed indexed fields equivalent to this domain-neutral example:

```json
{
  "record_type": "scheduled_action_projection",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_7s",
  "account_id": "acct_42",
  "workflow_id": "wf_nurture",
  "run_id": "job_9001",
  "instance_id": "inst_contact_001",
  "action_id": "act_001",
  "target_key": "contact:001",
  "action_type": "message.send",
  "status": "scheduled",
  "scheduled_at": "2026-07-02T14:00:00Z",
  "completed_at": null,
  "scheduler_algorithm": "personalized",
  "engagement_probability": 0.0825,
  "engagement_threshold": 0.10,
  "suppressed_by_recycling": true,
  "is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter": false,
  "payload": {"message_ref":"welcome_email","contact_open_rate_state":{"openRate":0.0825,"runningRate":0.096,"isOptOut":false}}
}
```

REQUIRED QUERY SHAPES
1. Detail page query: filter by tenant/account/run/action/status/scheduled range; order by scheduled_at, completed_at, status, scheduler_algorithm, engagement_probability, or stable id; return cursor-paginated rows.
2. Hourly distribution query: `tenant_id = T AND run_id = R AND action_type = message.send AND scheduled_at >= start AND scheduled_at < end GROUP BY hour(scheduled_at), status ORDER BY hour`.
3. Recycling preview query substrate: same scheduled range, grouped by hour and `suppressed_by_recycling`, with filter expressions over `engagement_probability`, `engagement_threshold`, and `is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter`.
4. Engagement segment query substrate: group by declared numeric buckets over `engagement_probability` (0, 0-1, 1-2, ..., 9-10, 10-15, ..., 95-100, no-activity).
5. Safe bounded mutation substrate: scan/update records for a run where `status = scheduled AND is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter = false`, setting status/suppression projection fields with per-record CAS or equivalent compare-and-set so concurrent claims/commits cannot lose updates.
6. Claim due work by query: claim records by `tenant_id/run_id/action_type/status/scheduled_at <= as_of` in scheduled_at order, returning lease tokens and item versions compatible with the existing claimed-work commit/finalize boundary.

EXPECTED INDEXES
At minimum, tests must define and exercise these typed compound indexes or equivalent query plans:
- `(tenant_id, run_id, scheduled_at)` range/order index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, status, scheduled_at)` pending/due/status index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, action_type, scheduled_at)` action distribution index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, suppressed_by_recycling, scheduled_at)` recycling bucket index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, scheduler_algorithm, scheduled_at)` algorithm bucket index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, engagement_probability)` numeric segment source index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, target_key)` unique lookup/upsert index.

EXAMPLE FIXTURE DATA
Seed at least these records in a shared conformance fixture:

```json
[
  {"action_id":"act_001","target_key":"contact:001","scheduled_at":"2026-07-02T14:05:00Z","status":"scheduled","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"personalized","engagement_probability":0.0825,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":true,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":false},
  {"action_id":"act_002","target_key":"contact:002","scheduled_at":"2026-07-02T14:37:00Z","status":"scheduled","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"personalized","engagement_probability":0.1280,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":false,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":true},
  {"action_id":"act_003","target_key":"contact:003","scheduled_at":"2026-07-02T15:02:00Z","status":"suppressed","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"randomized","engagement_probability":0.0000,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":true,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":false},
  {"action_id":"act_004","target_key":"contact:004","scheduled_at":"2026-07-02T15:45:00Z","status":"scheduled","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"randomized","engagement_probability":null,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":false,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":true},
  {"action_id":"act_005","target_key":"contact:005","scheduled_at":"2026-07-03T09:15:00Z","status":"failed","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"personalized","engagement_probability":0.4510,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":false,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":true},
  {"action_id":"act_006","target_key":"contact:006","scheduled_at":"2026-07-03T09:50:00Z","status":"scheduled","action_type":"subject.mutation","scheduler_algorithm":"personalized","engagement_probability":0.9100,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":false,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":true}
]
```

NON-SCOPE
- Snorri workflow API, Cayce MCP implementation, source-map rendering, and open-rate policy semantics.
- Niflheim/ClickHouse archival analytics.
- Arbitrary SQL/JSONPath/expression execution from callers.
- RESP-specific reporting surface unless the native Rust/query substrate is already proven.

FIX OPTIONS: a bounded due-sweep that refreshes group summaries whose next not_before has passed, OR discover candidate groups live from pqueue_items (DISTINCT group_key of currently-eligible items) ordered by a live rep (loses the summary's scale benefit), OR accept as a documented known-limitation. description:
PROBLEM
Bounded or interrupted partial expiry must leave undeleted below-floor manifest entries visible to later expiry and recovery. If enumeration uses the read horizon or logical floor as a manifest deletion boundary, partial expiry can hide objects that were not physically deleted. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec. Before implementation, evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring and document whether it would allow any cheaper delete-only variant.

ROOT CAUSE
crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1996 states that expire_segments_through deletes only segment objects. crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1998 deliberately does not delete manifest tombstones. crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2028 advances only the read horizon after reclamation. Enumeration that treats the read horizon as sufficient manifest deletion proof can skip below-floor entries that remain physically present after partial expiry.

PROPOSED FIX
Update manifest enumeration and expiry filtering to use the conservative manifest deletion watermark, not the read horizon alone, when deciding which below-floor manifest entries may be hidden. Ensure bounded expiry, interrupted expiry, and later full expiry all observe undeleted entries until the contiguous physical-deletion watermark has advanced past them.

NON-SCOPE
Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not hide not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, or projection storage. Do not implement a delete-only compaction on the current index-CAS protocol. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists. Do not implement sibling child acceptance criteria beyond enumeration and visibility behavior.

PROBLEM: Below-floor manifest objects are physically deleted, but delete-only reclamation can free the write-once manifest index address that stale-writer fencing relies on. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:365. Dependency ID: pqueue-c33c367e; the fix must not depend on pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring unless it proves a substrate-level bounded-staleness invariant.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:984 deletes manifest entries by removing both legacy and authoritative head objects; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:976 uses create-only `put_if_absent` as the manifest CAS; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1324 keeps the seal path on an in-memory cached tail and intentionally avoids listing the manifest before every seal. Freeing an old index can let a dormant stale writer win CAS at that freed address and false-ack.
PROPOSED FIX: Introduce a permanent below-floor fence marker for each reclaimed manifest index, or an equivalent substrate-visible tombstone state, so reclamation removes payload bytes without making the historical manifest index writable again. The manifest CAS must collide with or reject writes to fenced reclaimed indices as `EpochFenced` or `Conflict` without relying on tail-validate/delete rollback.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, projection storage, or release packaging. Do not accept tail-validate/delete rollback as a substitute for a permanent fence. Do not rely on pqueue-c33c367e unless this bead proves and documents the bounded-window invariant. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.
title: objectlog: reserve reclaimed manifest indices with permanent fence markers

description:
Deferred non-blocking follow-up from the retention-floor work (bead pqueue-b5cc2bc7), noted in crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs branch_with_emission. Branch creation is atomic via a commit marker (branch.json written LAST) + a branch.pending sentinel; an uncommitted branch is non-readable, so a partial/failed branch is safe (never reads a reclaimed segment). BUT a failed branch creation (or a rollback whose object cleanup itself failed) can leave ORPHAN objects on the store: a leftover branch.pending sentinel and/or partially-copied branch manifest/segment objects. These are harmless (non-readable, do not corrupt) but they are durable garbage that is never reclaimed — a slow space leak proportional to failed-branch-creation attempts.

SCOPE: implement GC for orphaned/uncommitted-branch objects — a branch whose commit marker (branch.json) is ABSENT but whose sentinel/objects are present, past a safety window, can have ALL its objects (sentinel, manifest, segments, floor entries) deleted. Must be safe: never delete objects of a COMMITTED branch (marker present) or an in-flight creation still within its window; coordinate with the branch pin so a live source pin from an in-flight creation is respected.

acceptance: 1. lease_decide_acquire preserves assignment_epoch when acquiring owner == current.active_owner; bumps only on different/none owner. 2. A different-owner takeover STILL bumps the epoch (fences superseded owner); existing fencing tests green. 3. A graceful-degradation test proves a lapsed-then-re-acquired same-owner lease keeps its epoch so in-flight writes are NOT fenced. 4. cargo test --workspace passes.
description: Under CPU starvation / high host load, multi-node object_log_sqlite_projection collapses ~36x (8-owner worst per-queue 3300/s -> 87/s) instead of degrading gracefully. ROOT CAUSE (code-traced): each node runs its own InMemoryControlPlane (sole owner of its disjoint queues). When the background renew_sessions task runs late under load, the lease TTL (15s) lapses; cp_resolve reports Unassigned; the node re-acquires via lease_decide_acquire (control_plane.rs:126) which UNCONDITIONALLY does assignment_epoch+1. That epoch bump fences the node's OWN in-flight pushes/claims (EpochFenced / -ERR pqueue epoch_stale) -> client retry storm -> under continued starvation repeats -> collapse. A slow-but-alive owner fences itself. FIX: re-affirming ownership of one's OWN uncontested lease (current.active_owner == acquiring owner) must PRESERVE assignment_epoch (refresh lease_expires_at only); epoch advances ONLY on takeover by a DIFFERENT owner. Safe: if the authority record still names us active_owner, no other owner acquired in the gap. Result: graceful degradation. Exposed by pqueue-36d405a9's live cargo test failing its 8-owner sweep under host load ~13 on a 12-core box.
title: Ownership self-fencing under load: re-acquiring own lease bumps the fence epoch (no graceful degradation)

description:
PROBLEM: A stale objectlog owner can restart with a cached reclaimed `next_manifest_index`; if reclaimed-index fence state is only process-local, reopen/recovery can permit a false ack at a historical index. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:365. Dependency ID: pqueue-c33c367e; this child must not depend on pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring unless it proves a substrate-level bounded-staleness invariant.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:984 deletes manifest entries by removing both legacy and authoritative head objects; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:976 uses create-only `put_if_absent` as the manifest CAS; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1324 keeps seal on an in-memory recovered tail and intentionally avoids manifest listing before every seal; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2220 reloads only the durable read-horizon blob, so any reclaimed-index fence state that is not persisted there or in an equivalent recovery-visible object is lost across reopen.
PROPOSED FIX: Persist reclaimed-index fence state in a recovery-visible objectlog substrate object and reload it during open/recovery before seal can accept a stale cached index. The stale writer must reject with `EpochFenced` or `Conflict` before writing a segment or manifest entry, while preserving the O(1) seal hot path shape from docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:365.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, projection storage, or release packaging. Do not accept tail-validate/delete rollback as a substitute for a permanent fence. Do not rely on pqueue-c33c367e unless this bead proves and documents the bounded-window invariant. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.

description:
Deferred non-blocking follow-up from the retention-floor work (bead pqueue-b5cc2bc7), noted in crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs branch_with_emission (~1420/1563). Branch creation uses pin-first + validate-after-copy: if the source retention floor MOVES during creation (a concurrent peer trim), the branch rolls back cleanly and returns EngineError::Conflict so the CALLER can retry against the advanced floor. Today the caller sees a bare Conflict and must retry manually. This is a usability gap, not a correctness one (fail-closed is safe).

SCOPE: make branch creation transparently retry (bounded, e.g. a few attempts) when it fails with Conflict due to a concurrent source-floor advance — re-read the advanced floor and re-attempt (or cleanly reject with cut <= floor if the cut is now below the floor). Keep it bounded (avoid livelock under continuous trimming) and preserve all the SOUND safety: pin-first, validate-after-copy, atomic commit marker, no missing-segment branch, no unpinned partial branch. Do NOT swallow a genuine cut<=floor rejection.

acceptance: 1. Manifest OBJECT COUNT (not just read cost) is bounded on a long-lived trimmed queue: below-floor manifest objects are physically reclaimed, keeping total manifest objects ~O(live)+O(recent-history). 2. The cross-owner stale-writer fence is PRESERVED without relying on the write-once index address space: a superseded/stale writer can never false-ack a phantom entry (proven by an adversarial test interleaving a compaction/deletion with a stale-epoch writer's commit). 3. AC-TXN-3 replay-across-restart, behind-image fail-closed, branch inheritance, and the retention floor all still hold. 4. Codex adversarial review APPROVES the new fencing/commit protocol. 5. rustup 1.92.0 cargo test across objectlog+sqlite+engine+conformance passes; fmt + clippy -D warnings clean.
description: Deferred Option 2 from the manifest-compaction design (bead pqueue-8928baec, closed; see docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md). The shipped read-horizon fix (pqueue-8928baec) bounds per-READ/recovery cost to live history but deliberately NEVER frees a manifest index address (the write-once put_if_absent index collision is the only stale-writer fence, and writer staleness is unbounded at the substrate), so manifest OBJECT COUNT + storage bytes still grow slowly as never-read below-horizon entries. Erik accepted that residual for now (read-cost was the operational pain). This bead is the larger change to bound object COUNT: replace the per-index-collision fence with a redesigned atomic fencing/commit protocol so manifest indices CAN be physically deleted safely — e.g. a PERMANENT linearizable head object (current epoch + next index) updated via conditional-update/CAS as the fence, plus UNIQUE per-attempt segment keys so a rolled-back/stale write cannot resurrect or clobber a live segment. That decouples the fence from the index address space, allowing true deletion of below-floor manifest objects (bounding read AND storage). HIGH blast radius: touches the core commit path (seal), recover_manifest (read head instead of list-max), branch manifest copy, epoch fencing, and needs a new BlobStore conditional-head primitive; own release + multi-round codex hardening. Only pursue if manifest object-count/storage growth becomes operationally real (very long-lived, high-write, trimming-enabled queues). Related root cause: pqueue ownership fence wiring (the c33c367e follow-up) — if a superseded owner were provably fenced within a bounded window < retention_ms, a cheaper delete-only compaction might become viable; evaluate that interaction first.

description:
Residual from pqueue-41bf00d7. That bead delivered SAFE terminal-item retention advancement for objectlog/hybrid-async (durable SQLite terminal rows reclaimed, gated by async-apply debt, id-resurrection-safe across the whole relational family, proven withhold->advance on durable state). What remains is object-log SEGMENT-OBJECT reclamation (trimming/expiring durable log segments to actually reclaim object storage), which is NOT safely achievable under the current recovery contract.

WHY IT'S BLOCKED (codex-confirmed, empirically verified): ComposedBackend recovery folds the object log FROM GENESIS (from=None) to rebuild BOTH the push and commit_transition request-id idempotency maps (compose.rs run_recovery ~1632/1730). Deleting any segment object breaks the genesis fold (reopen fails with "missing segment ...seg/..."); even a retention-floor read-clamp would drop request-ids still within request_id_retention_ms, REGRESSING the proven AC-TXN-3 unknown-outcome-replay-across-restart guarantee. There is no safe narrow segment trim.

SCOPE: a bounded-recovery redesign — a durable retention floor / snapshot the idempotency rebuild honors (so recovery can start above a trimmed horizon without losing in-retention request-ids), plus a trim horizon that never crosses the durable checkpoint OR the request_id retention window. Then implement segment-object expiry gated by the already-wired retention_may_advance (async-apply debt withholds it), and prove it end-to-end (segments reclaimed once debt clears AND request_id replay + recovery still hold across restart).

description:
PROBLEM: The manifest-head design needs explicit rollout constraints before implementation, especially deletion deferral, owner-fence evaluation, and the safety envelope around stale writers; otherwise later children may assume physical deletion is safe too early. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec; evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring before implementation and document whether it changes the deletion safety envelope.
ROOT CAUSE: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:21 explains that freeing an old index lets a stale writer win create-only CAS at that address; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:60 makes create-only put_if_absent the only CAS; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:55 defines BlobStore without a linearizable conditional-update/head primitive; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1010 derives (next_seq,next_manifest_index,current_epoch) by listing manifest keys and reading the max key.
PROPOSED FIX: Update docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md with rollout constraints for the permanent head approach, a pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence evaluation, and the explicit non-scope decision that physical deletion of manifest entries waits for later children. Document that the deletion safety envelope must not depend on an unproven wall-clock staleness bound. Keep docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374 explicitly referenced and keep dependency ID pqueue-8928baec visible.
NON-SCOPE: Do not implement physical deletion of manifest entries in this child. Do not change branch copy semantics beyond reading/recovering the head-compatible tail. Do not relax AC-TXN-3 replay, behind-image fail-closed, branch inheritance, retention floor, or epoch fencing. Do not depend on an unproven wall-clock staleness bound; pqueue-c33c367e must be evaluated first, not assumed. Do not squash/rebase/filter DDX attempt history. Do not implement code changes; this child is documentation-only.
title: objectlog: document rollout constraints and deletion deferral for manifest head
