description:
PROBLEM: A stale owner frozen on an old epoch/index can currently resume after another owner advances the log and old manifest indices are deleted, because the stale-writer fence is tied to the deletable index object rather than the permanent head CAS. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec; evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring before implementation and document whether it can bound stale writers inside retention.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1264 fences only against the in-memory `buf.committed_epoch`; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1281 writes deterministic segment keys from `first_seq`; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1300 commits via `put_if_absent` at `manifest/{cur_index}`; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1302 handles CAS loss by rereading the manifest tail. docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 rejects tail-validate rollback because deterministic segment keys and reader-visible manifest commits make rollback unsafe.
PROPOSED FIX: Add the stale-writer rejection path and adversarial regression coverage for a frozen owner resuming after the permanent head has advanced and old manifest indices have been compacted/deleted. The resumed stale attempt must fail as `EpochFenced` or `Conflict` before acknowledging any phantom entry, and any unreachable attempt objects must remain non-published garbage that cannot clobber live data.
NON-SCOPE: Do not implement below-floor manifest deletion here except for any unreachable failed-attempt cleanup required by the new protocol. Do not change projection apply semantics, request-id replay, branch creation, retention policy, or release packaging. Do not accept tail-validate/delete rollback as a substitute for head CAS. Do not rely on pqueue-c33c367e unless this bead proves and documents the bounded-window invariant.
title: objectlog: reject stale seal writers after manifest-index deletion

description:
PROBLEM: After segment expiry, manifest tombstones are retained forever, so object count and metadata bytes grow with lifetime writes even though read cost is bounded by the read horizon. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec. Depends on the durable manifest deletion watermark child bead from this decomposition. Evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring before implementation and document whether it would allow any cheaper delete-only variant.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1996 states that expire_segments_through deletes only segment objects; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1998 deliberately does not delete manifest tombstones; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2028 advances only the read horizon after reclamation; docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 records the residual that object count still grows because addresses are never freed.
PROPOSED FIX: Add the manifest-object reclamation pass that physically deletes manifest objects strictly below the retention/read floor once their data segments are reclaimed and no live branch pins them. Advance the persisted manifest deletion watermark only after successful deletion progress. Keep permanent head as the stale-writer fence and preserve fail-closed reads below the durable floor.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not hide not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, or projection storage. Do not implement a delete-only compaction on the current index-CAS protocol. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.

acceptance: Sink enabled on an unwired profile OR over a no-op cursor store fails startup with a structured error (regression test: kafka:// + no durable cursor = refused); queues/flags sourced dynamically from the control plane; tail read off the commit mutex (evidence); sink I/O non-blocking; workspace green.
description: Recreation of pqueue-e76ecc46, whose tracker row was deleted by worker tracker commit 0ab6218 (incident #4 on ddx-b31f46c6). Scope: the change-record emitter must fail closed. (1) Emitter spawns only on objectlog/hybrid profiles; every other backend silently ignores PQUEUE_CHANGE_RECORD_SINK_ENABLED=true — fail startup with a structured error instead. (2) Queue set is a static boot snapshot and per-queue emit_change_records is unreachable from server config — source both from the control plane. (3) Tail read holds the commit mutex during log.read_from (S3 reads would stall commits) — move it off the lock. (4) Sink does blocking TCP on tokio workers — spawn_blocking or async I/O. (5) CRITICAL (from review of c46bb3c4): a kafka:// endpoint constructs the fjord emitter UNGATED atop the non-durable emission cursor (P0 pqueue-657e5f8d) — every 250ms tick re-reads from genesis and re-produces the first 256 records forever into a memory-only topic (unbounded memory + livelock). Constructing ANY emitter over a no-op cursor store MUST be a hard startup error (or explicit unstable flag) until the durable cursor lands.
title: Change-record emitter fail-closed gating (recreates e76ecc46, deleted by worker tracker clobber)

description: Residual from pqueue-48a4af85 / commit aec2f3f5. rebuild_commit_idempotency_from_log reconstructs commit_transition's commit_idempotency cache from the durable log, but a REJECTED entry mutates nothing and appends nothing durable, so a commit that mixed committed+rejected entries reconstructs ONLY its committed, Finalize-delimited entries — a shorter Vec<EntryRecovery> than the live record. This is currently SAFE (not silently replayed): commit_transition's replay path guards on recovery.len()==entries.len(), so a short reconstructed record falls through to 0-duplicate re-execution rather than returning a misleading short outcome vec (committed inputs stay finalized exactly once). But it is NOT a faithful replay of the original per-entry vec. The full fix requires durably recording per-entry REJECTION outcomes on the commit (a wire-format / error-serialization change deliberately deferred from aec2f3f5 as pre-release risk, since it touches the shared CommandEnvelope across all backend crates). Also affects explain_commit, which returns only the committed subset for a reconstructed mixed commit.
title: AC-TXN-3 residual: faithful mixed committed+rejected commit_transition replay across restart (durable rejection records)

Preserve ack-after-commit and stale epoch rejection.

description: Follow-ups from review of c46bb3c4 (findings 5/6/8). (1) Topic mapping fjord_topic_name uses '.' separator: tenant 'a.b'/queue 'c' collides with tenant 'a'/queue 'b.c' (cross-tenant record mixing + authz confusion); tenant/queue IDs also unvalidated against Kafka-illegal chars — validate/escape the mapping and reject ambiguous IDs. (2) Endpoint conflation: the sink endpoint doubles as the embedded broker BIND address, so ADR-014's external-Kafka deployment mode is unexpressible (pointing at an external broker makes pqueue try to bind it; bind fails but the TCP readiness probe can succeed against the real broker, masking the dead embedded task). (3) Wire hygiene: pq-command-kind header uses Rust Debug formatting as a wire contract — pin explicit serialization; per-record sequential blocking produce (10s timeout each) via block_in_place inside the tick (panics on current-thread runtime) — batch/async produce; remove the magic 400ms startup sleep; tests should assert the record-key format and pq-item-id.

description:
PROBLEM
Partial expiry needs a manifest deletion watermark that is independent from the read horizon. Advancing manifest deletion state based only on logical expiry can hide below-floor manifest entries that were not physically deleted, which breaks later full expiry and recovery. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec. Before implementation, evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring and document whether it would allow any cheaper delete-only variant.

ROOT CAUSE
crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1996 states that expire_segments_through deletes only segment objects. crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1998 deliberately does not delete manifest tombstones. crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2028 advances only the read horizon after reclamation. Without separate conservative manifest deletion bookkeeping, partial expiry can move manifest visibility past below-floor entries that are still present and still needed by later expiry or recovery.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce persisted or reconstructable manifest deletion watermark bookkeeping that is separate from the read horizon. The watermark must advance only through a contiguous prefix of manifest objects that are physically deleted, unpinned, and below the expiry floor. Wire the new state into expiry metadata without changing branch pin semantics or legacy bootstrap behavior.

NON-SCOPE
Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not hide not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, or projection storage. Do not implement a delete-only compaction on the current index-CAS protocol. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists. Do not implement sibling child acceptance criteria beyond the state/bookkeeping slice.
title: objectlog: add manifest deletion watermark state for partial expiry

description:
PROBLEM: `acquire_epoch` must participate in the same permanent head-CAS fence as `seal`; otherwise a new owner can start writing data before the durable head reflects ownership, leaving stale old-epoch or future-epoch appends insufficiently fenced. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec; evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring before implementation and document whether it can bound stale writers inside retention.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1264 fences only against the in-memory `buf.committed_epoch`; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1281 writes deterministic segment keys from `first_seq`; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1300 commits via `put_if_absent` at `manifest/{cur_index}`; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1302 handles CAS loss by rereading the manifest tail. docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 rejects tail-validate rollback because deterministic segment keys and reader-visible manifest commits make rollback unsafe.
PROPOSED FIX: Redesign `acquire_epoch` so the permanent manifest head is advanced as the ownership fence before the new owner can write data. Preserve rejection of stale old-epoch and invalid future-epoch appends as `EpochFenced`, and keep the protocol compatible with the unique attempt segment key scheme used by `seal`.
NON-SCOPE: Do not implement below-floor manifest deletion here except for any unreachable failed-attempt cleanup required by the new protocol. Do not change projection apply semantics, request-id replay, branch creation, retention policy, or release packaging. Do not accept tail-validate/delete rollback as a substitute for head CAS. Do not rely on pqueue-c33c367e unless this bead proves and documents the bounded-window invariant.
title: objectlog: make acquire_epoch advance the permanent head fence

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead pqueue-01d51100 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 2 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: The completed head-CAS compaction protocol needs release-grade evidence across objectlog, sqlite, engine, conformance, workspace quality gates, dependency interaction notes, and Codex adversarial review before the parent bead can close. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374 and docs/helix/03-test/test-plans/TP-003-verification-acceptance-criteria.md:224. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec; evaluate pqueue-c33c367e interaction first and carry that conclusion into release notes.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1693, crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1755, crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1772, and crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1826 span branch inheritance, manifest recovery, floor seeding, and branch epoch acquisition. The protocol's blast radius requires explicit review of head CAS linearizability, stale writers, branch pins, partial expiry, restart replay, and S3/MinIO semantics, plus reproducible release gates.
PROPOSED FIX: Run the full release matrix and quality gates, document pqueue-c33c367e interaction conclusions in release notes, run Codex adversarial review on the final fencing/commit protocol, fix blocking findings or map them to follow-up beads, and preserve evidence for all verification requirements.
NON-SCOPE: Do not introduce new queue semantics or user-facing API changes. Do not relax existing branch atomicity, orphan GC, source pin, retention floor, or fail-closed guarantees. Do not skip objectlog, sqlite, engine, conformance, fmt, clippy, lefthook, go test, or Codex adversarial review gates. Do not pursue this work unless manifest object-count/storage growth is operationally real for very long-lived, high-write, trimming-enabled queues.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- TestRustReleaseMatrixGate: run rustup 1.92.0 cargo test -p pqueue-objectlog -- --nocapture, rustup 1.92.0 cargo test -p pqueue-sqlite -- --nocapture, rustup 1.92.0 cargo test -p pqueue-engine -- --nocapture, rustup 1.92.0 cargo test -p pqueue-conformance -- --nocapture, and rustup 1.92.0 cargo test --workspace.
- TestWorkspaceQualityGate: run cargo +1.92.0 fmt --all --check, cargo +1.92.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, go test ./... (record not-applicable if no Go module/packages exist), lefthook run pre-commit (or record missing lefthook config/tool as an operator-required gate failure), and scripts/ci/pr-gate.sh enforcing if available.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.
title: objectlog: release hardening and adversarial review for head compaction: part 2

description: PROBLEM: spawn_embedded_fjord_broker builds its own EmbeddedFjordSurface and returns only a JoinHandle (crates/pqueue-server/src/lib.rs:377); start() builds a SEPARATE surface it discards (lib.rs:1217). A sink appending to a different surface would not feed the broker consumers. ROOT CAUSE: surface ownership is not shared between the broker task and the sink. PROPOSED FIX: construct one EmbeddedFjordSurface in start(), own its Arc<dyn LogBackend>, and hand it BOTH to HeimqServer AND to the FjordChangeRecordSink so in-process appends are visible to broker fetches. NON-SCOPE: record-batch encoding (B0.1c), config-mode split (B0.1e); no external-kafka path.
title: Share embedded fjord broker log handle with the change-record sink

description:
PROBLEM: Read and recovery paths must not use the deletion watermark to hide missing or torn live manifest entries above the watermark, at/above the durable floor, or during partial expiry. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:366 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:367. Dependency ID: pqueue-c33c367e; evaluate and document that this watermark does not rely on owner-fence wiring.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2205 can recover the read horizon, crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2225 derives the authoritative retention floor from the manifest, and crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:984 can remove manifest entries, but missing-entry handling lacks explicit guardrails separating intentional below-floor deletion from live-entry corruption or partial expiry.
PROPOSED FIX: Add read/recovery checks that preserve existing error behavior for absent manifest entries above the deletion watermark, at or above the authoritative durable floor, or below the floor but not yet durably deleted. Ensure the watermark never masks not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry and never becomes retention-floor authority.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, projection storage, or release packaging. Do not use the watermark to hide not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry. Do not make the watermark an authority for retention floor advancement. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.
title: objectlog: keep missing live manifest entries visible despite watermark

description:
PROBLEM: Manifest objects below the retention floor cannot be physically deleted while a live branch still pins their source segments; reclamation must become eligible only after the branch is discarded or expires. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec; evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring before implementation and document whether it would allow any cheaper delete-only variant.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1996 states that expire_segments_through deletes only segment objects; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1998 deliberately does not delete manifest tombstones; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2028 advances only the read horizon after reclamation; the proposed reclamation must additionally account for branch-pinned source segments before deleting manifest entries.
PROPOSED FIX: Gate manifest-object deletion on the existing branch pin/liveness checks so pinned source segment manifests remain available. After pin release, allow the next compaction/reclamation pass to delete newly unpinned below-floor manifest objects while preserving the permanent head stale-writer fence.
NON-SCOPE: Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not hide not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, or projection storage. Do not implement a delete-only compaction on the current index-CAS protocol. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.
title: objectlog: honor branch pins during manifest-object reclamation
